legacy_root.question: Enumerate the [REDACTED] dispatch failures already measured on this estate - fire-and-forget background dispatch that loses the result, Windows 32,767-character command-line overflow, a progress stream mistaken for a result, and typed output-schema failures while MCP tools are active - and specify the adapter-level guard for each plus its terminal-state marker, so every dispatch ends in SUCCESS:<id> or FAILED:<id> <reason> and never in silence.

scenario.catching_architecture: [REDACTED] adapter.dispatch: refuse --background, refuse inline argv over the conservative UTF-16 threshold, classify progress-only as severed-stream, enforce output_schema even when MCP tools are active, and emit SUCCESS:<id> or FAILED:<id> <reason> from every dispatch return point.
procedure: 1. Reproduce fire-and-forget: set background=True and --background; assert FAILED fire-and-forget. Run wait=True without the flag; assert SUCCESS. Run a body that only discusses background work; assert SUCCESS (use-vs-mention).

2. Reproduce win-arg-limit: assemble an inline prompt of 34,472 characters (estate payload_len) and assert assembled UTF-16 exceeds 32,767 and the guard fires. The same payload via --prompt-file stays under the cap and SUCCESS. This Linux box does not re-hit CreateProcess 206.
3. Reproduce progress-as-result: feed a PROGRESS object and a PROGRESS NDJSON stream; assert FAILED severed-stream. A typed receipt body is SUCCESS.
4. Reproduce schema-invalid with MCP active: invalid body + mcp_tools_active=True must FAIL schema-invalid; the same valid body with MCP on is SUCCESS. MCP must not skip the schema check.
5. AST-walk dispatch and _checked; every Return must call terminal(). Inject return None into _checked and assert the enumerator fails.
